results.title: SA client identity consistency (spec OSG-KCLT-01)
results.desc: Token audience/azp must agree with the stored client_id; gateway must accept
results.detail: client_id=hs-sa-3LjHZXxh1VxJwUjDzZ6cR7J3p1X-3LjHpkuEpxRdLhNj59m76xgl0Z0; JWT aud=3LjHZXxh1VxJwUjDzZ6cR7J3p1X (the bare GATEWAY ID); azp=client_id (exact); iss=keycloak hypershell realm; gateway Health accepts token (grpc=0 all cycle)
results.prose: Random spec draw: openshell-gateway-keycloak.transitional.spec.md (OSG-KCLT-01) — gateway-owned client IDs used exactly as stored, client_id and audience agreeing. My first assertion was wrong (I expected SA aud == SA client_id) and the failure taught the real topology: for sandbox service accounts, the JWT audience is the bare GATEWAY ID (3LjHZXxh…) while azp names the SA client exactly — the SA authenticates as itself, authorized toward that gateway. The gateway accepts these tokens on every RPC this cycle. The spec's agree-both-ways rule is about the gateway's own client; the SA layer sits one hop outside it, targeting the gateway as audience.
results.steps: Read SA env client_id; request fresh client-credentials token; base64-decode JWT payload; compare aud/azp to client_id; call gateway Health RPC with the token.
